@copilot Update this PR directly to follow the Apache Dubbo semantic conventions, rather than classifying failures by RpcException's integer codes. Preserve this existing PR's draft/ready state and update its title and description to reflect the resulting behavior. Do not create a separate follow-up PR.

The user directed "we should follow semconv", then "proceed", and has now requested cloud execution. The discussed cap of 100 was only an earlier suggestion, not the goal. Remove the assumption that the currently defined RpcException codes 1-13, or an arbitrary larger cap, are protocol response statuses.

Use the released v1.44.0 Dubbo convention, matching the RPC-preview schema currently emitted by RpcCommonAttributesExtractor: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/rpc/dubbo.md. When a protocol response status indicates an error, error.type SHOULD use the protocol status name. Without a status, use the exception's fully qualified class name or a justified component-specific, low-cardinality identifier. Keep error.type absent on successful operations. Capture the actual status, not a guessed mapping from RpcException.getCode(); where status is captured, emit rpc.response.status_code with the protocol status name as specified by that version of the convention. Keep error classification consistent between spans and preview duration metrics, and apply the role-specific client/server error-status rules.

Investigate both native Dubbo and Triple across the module's supported versions. The shared filter boundary receives org.apache.dubbo.rpc.Result, not the native response envelope. In Dubbo 2.7.5, org.apache.dubbo.remoting.exchange.support.DefaultFuture.doReceived(Response) sees Response.getStatus() but converts non-OK responses into TimeoutException or RemotingException before the filter sees them, losing the exact status in many cases. Capture the actual native status before that conversion where feasible. In Dubbo 3.2.20 Triple, UnaryClientCallListener.onClose(TriRpcStatus, ...) converts an error status with status.asException(); org.apache.dubbo.rpc.StatusRpcException.getStatus() preserves the original TriRpcStatus, while inherited RpcException.getCode() is only a lossy translation. Use the preserved protocol status where available, with supported-version-compatible handling; verify other supported Triple versions rather than assuming that API exists everywhere. Do not conflate RpcException.NETWORK_EXCEPTION/TIMEOUT_EXCEPTION integer values with response statuses.

Relevant code starts in instrumentation/apache-dubbo-2.7/library-autoconfigure/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/apachedubbo/v2_7/DubboRpcAttributesGetter.java, TracingFilter.java, and DubboTelemetryBuilder.java, plus the javaagent module and the shared testing/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/apachedubbo/v2_7/AbstractDubboTest.java. Trace operation completion and async callbacks so status is captured before telemetry ends. Preserve default legacy telemetry, RPC-preview and duplicate-mode behavior, baseline/latest dependency compatibility, and both standalone library and javaagent operation. Do not make the library require javaagent transformation. If a supported library/protocol boundary cannot expose its actual status, retain the semconv exception-type fallback there and explain the concrete limitation in the PR description instead of inventing a status or claiming full status capture.

Extend the existing shared real provider/consumer integration coverage, including representative native Dubbo and Triple status-bearing failures, failures without a status, synchronous/asynchronous completion, client/server spans, preview duration metric error types, and successful operations. Reuse existing success and semconv suites instead of duplicating them, and do not resurrect the removed mocked filter matrix or removed getter unit-test file. Follow repository instructions, apply the narrowest applicable spotlessApply before behavior validation, run relevant targeted library/javaagent suites and baseline/latest variants where feasible, and state any actual validation blockers. Acceptance is semconv-based protocol-status classification where obtainable, meaningful exception fallback otherwise, no numeric exception-code allowlist, no fabricated or message-parsed statuses, and regression coverage through real supported RPC paths.

Capture the actual native Response.getStatus() and report its defined protocol status name in rpc.response.status_code; use that status name as error.type when the role-specific status rules classify the operation as an error. Clients treat every status except OK as an error; native Dubbo server error statuses are SERVER_ERROR, SERVER_THREADPOOL_EXHAUSTED_ERROR, SERVER_TIMEOUT, and SERVICE_ERROR. Keep error.type absent for successful operations and keep spans and preview duration metric error classification consistent. Do not confuse protocol statuses with RpcException.getCode(), guess status from that lossy code, parse exception messages, or introduce the previously discussed arbitrary numeric cap.

The shared org.apache.dubbo.rpc.Filter/Result boundary is too late to recover many native statuses. In the verified Dubbo 2.7.5 implementation, org.apache.dubbo.remoting.exchange.support.DefaultFuture.doReceived(Response) can read Response.getStatus(), then completes with the response result or converts failures into TimeoutException/RemotingException, losing the exact status before TracingFilter receives it. Trace the concrete supported-version implementations and capture the native status before it is discarded, using protocol-level javaagent hooks where necessary rather than stopping at the filter limitation again. threads.body: [General] In RPC-preview mode, a native Dubbo transport timeout or disconnect can abort telemetry completion here. `TracingFilter` passes both the failed `AsyncRpcResult` and the transport throwable to `instrumenter.end`. In Dubbo 3.3.6, `AsyncRpcResult.getException()` calls `getAppResponse()`, which throws `RpcException` when its response future completed exceptionally. Since the transport throwable has no Triple status, this fallback invokes that accessor and exits `Instrumenter.doEndImpl` before applying end attributes, setting error status, or recording duration metrics. Inspect the response only when no throwable was supplied, retaining exception-class fallback otherwise. Add a real client transport-timeout regression; throwing `RpcException.TIMEOUT_EXCEPTION` inside the provider does not exercise an exceptionally completed response future.

replies.body: Fixed in a33418a2. A supplied callback throwable now takes precedence, so status extraction does not inspect the failed AsyncRpcResult. Result-only failures still use the response exception. The shared real-RPC timeout regression holds the provider until the client times out, then verifies the completed client error span and preview duration metric.

The user explicitly approved this follow-up after the latest Copilot review identified that DubboRpcStatus.getStatusCodeFromException checks the exact exception class name. Reuse existing reflected metadata where practical, for example the declaring class of GET_STATUS with isInstance, instead of adding duplicate type discovery. Preserve absence handling on Dubbo 2.7, optional Triple compatibility, loader awareness, transport-error precedence, CompletionException-only cycle-safe unwrapping, and exception-class fallback for unrelated failures. Keep all status classification rules and the newly approved semantic-conventions comment unchanged; do not emit rpc.status_code.
